lead.text: For a typical customer (in West Virginia, with no international plan, no voice-mail plan, one call to customer service and about 180 daytime minutes), the model predicts a chance of about {{C001.risk.from|pct}} that the customer leaves; it adds up three parts: daytime use and service calls, a set of direct terms, and a few small state terms.

sentences.text: This part combines daytime charge, evening charge, voice-mail and customer-service calls, and its pieces add up.

A higher daytime charge raises the predicted chance that a customer leaves in an uneven way, and even more so if {{C115.statement.stronger_group.cond|text}}: for a typical customer (with daytime minutes moved along with the charge, and evening minutes set to match the group), going from {{C115.statement.change.from}} to {{C115.statement.change.to}} moves it from about {{C115.risk.groups[0].from|pct}} to about {{C115.risk.groups[0].to|pct}} in that group, and from about {{C115.risk.groups[1].from|pct}} to about {{C115.risk.groups[1].to|pct}} otherwise.

Many calls to customer service add to it in an uneven way from about {{C096.shape.point.text|text}} upwards (between {{C096.shape.point.spread_text[0]|text}} and {{C096.shape.point.spread_text[1]|text}} for different customers; for {{C096.statement.support_check.exceptions}} of the {{C096.statement.support_check.n}} training customers it already acts below that): for a typical customer, going from {{C096.statement.change.from}} to {{C096.statement.change.to}} moves it from about {{C096.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C096.risk.to|pct}}.

Daytime minutes add to it in stages once they rise above about {{C107.statement.threshold.text|text}}, checked for every one of the {{C107.statement.support_check.n}} training customers without a voice-mail plan: for a typical such customer (with daytime charge moved along), going from {{C107.statement.change.from}} to {{C107.statement.change.to}} moves it from about {{C107.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C107.risk.to|pct}}.
These terms add up independently, and the formula reproduces the part exactly.
For a typical customer, an international plan raises the predicted chance that a customer leaves from about {{C067.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C067.risk.to|pct}}.

The state matters too: compared with the typical customer's West Virginia, it is about {{C068.risk.to|pct}} in California and about {{C069.risk.to|pct}} in Washington, and {{C072.risk.to|pct}} in Vermont.

A voice-mail plan lowers it from about {{C074.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C074.risk.to|pct}} (with the number of voice-mail messages moved along); voice-mail messages and the plan also act through the part above.

These small terms mostly shift the chance for customers in a few states: for a typical customer, it is about {{C125.risk.to|pct}} in Utah rather than about {{C125.risk.from|pct}}, and about {{C126.risk.to|pct}} in North Dakota.
